speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and sexual activity with multiple female partners, have you been diagnosed with HIV, and do you experience jaundice or dark urine? text: RESULTS: HIV_Antibogen: Not reported in provided data; Hepatitis_C_Antibody: Not reported in provided data; Liver_Function_Panel: Hemoglobin 11.5 g/dL, Leukocyte_Count 7500/mm3, Platelet_Count 280,000/mm3, Na 138 mEq/L, K 4.7 mEq/L, Bilirubin_Total 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase 460 U/L, AST 75 U/L, ALT 78 U/L, Anti-Nuclear_Antibody Negative, Antimitochondrial_Antibodies Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: The labs show a significant elevation in Alkaline Phosphatase with mild bilirubin and normal AST/ALT, suggesting a cholestatic pattern. Given your history of ulcerative colitis, do you have a history of inflammatory bowel disease-associated primary sclerosing cholangitis, or do you notice pale, clay-colored stools? I am requesting images of a liver ultrasound and MRCP to evaluate for biliary dilation or strictures. REQUEST IMAGES: Liver_Ultrasound, MRCP

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the severe pruritus, scleral icterus, and the cholestatic liver pattern (high Alkaline Phosphatase) in a patient with Ulcerative Colitis, I am highly suspicious for Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC). The MRCP images I requested should show the "beads on a string" appearance characteristic of this condition. Have you noticed any fever, right upper quadrant pain, or weight loss alongside these symptoms?
